source_text:
1, Τὰς κακοτεχνίας φεῦγε, μᾶλλον δὲ περὶ τούτων ὁμιλίαν ποιοῦ. ταῖς ἀδελφαῖς μου προσλάλει, ἀγαπᾶν τὸν κύριον καὶ τοῖς συμβίοις ἀρκεῖσθαι σαρκὶ καὶ πνεύματι. ὁμοίως καὶ τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς μου παράγγελλε ἐν ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἀγαπᾶν τὰς συμβίους ὡς ὁ κύριος τὴν ἐκκλησίαν.
εἵ τις δύναται ἐν ἁγνείᾳ μένειν εἰς τιμὴν τῆς σαρκὸς τοῦ κυρίου, ἐν ἀκαυχησίᾳ μενέτω. ἐὰν καυχήσηται, ἀπώλετο, καὶ ἐὰν γνωσθῇ πλέον τοῦ ἐπισκόπου, ἔφθαρται. πρέπει δὲ τοῖς γαμοῦσι καὶ ταῖς γαμουμέναις μετὰ γνώμης τοῦ ἐπισκόπου τὴν ἕνωσιν ποιεῖσθαι, ἵνα ὁ γάμος ᾖ κατὰ κύριον καὶ μὴ κατ’ ἐπιθυμίαν. πάντα εἰς τιμὴν θεοῦ γινέσθω.
thought_title: Marriage, Purity, and the Bishop's Approval
orientation: Ignatius is giving instructions to Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna, about how to teach the brothers and sisters in his church regarding marriage and purity.
pass_a_gloss: The evil arts flee, but rather about these [things] a talk make. To my sisters speak kindly, to love the Lord and with [their] spouses to be content in flesh and in spirit. Likewise also to my brothers command in [the] name of Jesus Christ, to love [their] spouses as the Lord [loves] the church. If anyone is able in purity to remain for [the] honor of the flesh of the Lord, in [a state of] no boasting let him remain. If he boasts, he has perished, and if he is known more than the bishop, he has been corrupted. It is fitting but for the marrying [men] and the marrying [women] with [the] judgment of the bishop the union to make, so that the marriage may be according to [the] Lord and not according to desire. All [things] for [the] honor of God let happen.

choices.why: The noun means crafty or wicked practices; 'evil arts' keeps the sense of deliberate cunning without modernizing to 'heresies' or 'schemes'.
The verb implies addressing someone in a gentle, encouraging way; 'speak kindly to' captures the pastoral tone Ignatius wants from Polycarp.
The middle voice means to be satisfied or content with what one has; 'to be content with' preserves the sense of sufficiency in one's spouse.

choices.english: in a state of no boasting
choices.why: The noun is a rare compound meaning absence of boasting; the phrase keeps the negative force explicit rather than collapsing it into 'humility'.
The noun means considered opinion or approval; 'judgment' preserves the deliberative sense of the bishop's decision rather than a mere 'permission'.
The glossary term for church unity is used here for marriage; 'union' keeps the same English word across both contexts, showing Ignatius's parallel between ecclesial and marital unity.

bible_refs.note: ἀγαπᾶν τὰς συμβίους ὡς ὁ κύριος τὴν ἐκκλησίαν

pass_b_english: Flee from evil arts, and rather speak about these things. Speak kindly to my sisters, telling them to love the Lord and to be content with their husbands in flesh and spirit. Likewise command my brothers in the name of Jesus Christ to love their wives as the Lord loves the church.

If anyone is able to remain in continence for the honor of the Lord's flesh, let him remain without boasting. If he boasts, he has perished; and if he is esteemed more highly than the bishop, he has been corrupted. It is fitting for men and women who marry to make their union with the bishop's judgment, so that the marriage may be according to the Lord and not according to desire. Let all things be done for the honor of God.

problems.quote: to be content with their spouses
problems.why: ἀρκεῖσθαι means 'be content with' in sense of sufficiency, but context demands 'be content to live with' or 'remain with' spouses, not general satisfaction.
problems.fix: to be content to live with their spouses
problems.ruling: ἀρκεῖσθαι = ‘to be sufficient for’, not ‘to be content with’, changes sense

problems.quote: If he becomes known beyond the bishop
problems.why: γνωσθῇ here means 'become known' in sense of 'be recognized/approved' or possibly 'make himself known' as seeking recognition; 'beyond' misrepresents πλέον as spatial rather than 'more than/more highly than.'
problems.fix: if he is recognized more highly than the bishop
problems.ruling: πλέον τοῦ ἐπισκόπου = ‘more than the bishop’, not spatial ‘beyond’

edits.old: to be content with their spouses
edits.new: to be content to live with their spouses

edits.old: if he becomes known beyond the bishop
edits.new: if he is recognized more highly than the bishop

problems.quote: to be content to live with their spouses
problems.why: συμβίος = spouse/husband in both clauses; 'live with' adds notion absent from ἀρκεῖσθαι (be content with)
problems.fix: to be content with their husbands
problems.ruling: adds ‘live with’ not in ἀρκεῖσθαι (be content)

problems.why: Citation added by translator; no scripture citation in source. While alluding to Eph 5:25, adding it violates source text
problems.ruling: adds unsupported scripture citation not in source

edits.old: to be content to live with their spouses
edits.new: to be content with their husbands

edits.old: as the Lord loves the church (Ephesians 5:25).
edits.new: as the Lord loves the church.

fixed: Changed 'to be content to live with their spouses' to 'to be content with their husbands' to match ἀρκεῖσθαι (be content with) without adding 'live with'.
Removed the added parenthetical citation '(Ephesians 5:25)' since the source has no scripture citation.

problems.why: 'Evil arts' in 5.6, 7.5 likely translates same root as 'magic' in 1.19 (pharmakeia/mageia), but reader cannot connect these.
problems.fix: Use consistent translation or cross-reference in notes.

fixed: The English already says 'evil arts,' which is a valid translation of the source's κακοτεχνίας, but the checker notes it should be consistent with 'magic' used elsewhere for the same root. Changed to 'magic' to maintain consistency.

problems.quote: If he is esteemed more highly than the bishop, he has been corrupted
problems.why: Logic is compressed: continence boasted of above bishop's authority corrupts.
problems.fix: 'If he boasts of being more highly esteemed than the bishop'.

edits.old: if he is esteemed more highly than the bishop
edits.new: if he is known more than the bishop

fixed: The English 'if he is esteemed more highly than the bishop' misstates the source γνωσθῇ πλέον τοῦ ἐπισκόπου, which means 'if he is known more than the bishop' (i.e., if he becomes known beyond what the bishop knows or approves). The suggested fix 'If he boasts of being more highly esteemed than the bishop' adds 'boasts of' not in the source. Changed to 'if he is known more than the bishop' to match the Greek.

last_rejected.why: Should be 'not even talk about them' or 'avoid discussion'; 'rather make conversation' contradicts φεῦγε
last_rejected.fix: rather not even speak of them
last_rejected.ruling: Greek says ‘make conversation about these things’; translation matches contrast with ‘φεῦγε’.

last_rejected.quote: in a state of no boasting
last_rejected.why: 'No boasting' misses the sense; ἀκαυχησία means 'without boasting' or 'humility', but 'state of no boasting' is awkward and unclear
last_rejected.ruling: ‘ἐν ἀκαυχησίᾳ’ literally ‘in no boasting’; rendering is literal though clunky.

last_rejected.quote: recognized more highly than the bishop
last_rejected.why: 'Recognized' is wrong sense; γνωσθῇ here means 'known' in sense of 'become known/publicly prominent', i.e., 'become known beyond the bishop' = get ahead of/overshadow
last_rejected.fix: if he becomes known above the bishop
last_rejected.ruling: ‘γνωσθῇ πλέον τοῦ ἐπισκόπου’ = ‘be known more than the bishop’; translation conveys same sense.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'unity' for ἕνωσις; 'union' used instead for marriage context
last_rejected.ruling: ‘ἕνωσιν’ can mean ‘union’; using it for marriage is appropriate despite glossary note.

last_rejected.quote: telling them to love the Lord and to be content with their husbands in flesh and spirit
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀγαπᾶν τὸν κύριον καὶ τοῖς συμβίοις ἀρκεῖσθαι σαρκὶ καὶ πνεύματι
last_rejected.why: Adds ‘husbands’ and ‘content’, changing the meaning of ‘συμβίοι’ (cohabitants) and ‘ἀρκεῖσθαι’ (to be sufficient).
last_rejected.fix: telling them to love the Lord and to be sufficient for their cohabitants in flesh and spirit
last_rejected.ruling: συμβίοις in context means husbands; ἀρκεῖσθαι standardly means 'be content' (LSJ). Normal range.

polish.changed: Clarified the ascetic instruction by rendering 'in a state of no boasting' as 'without boasting,' making the contrast between celibacy and pride clearer while preserving every claim and qualification.

notes.quote: remain in a state of no boasting
notes.why: Ascetic practice of celibacy; 'no boasting' obscures technical term for unmarried state.
notes.fix: Clarify: 'Those who choose celibacy must not boast of it.'

polish.changed: Clarified 'purity' as 'continence' for the technical sense of sexual abstinence, replaced weak 'recognized' with 'esteemed,' and smoothed sentence flow while preserving every claim and reference.

notes.quote: If anyone is able to remain in purity for the honor of the Lord's flesh
notes.why: Refers to celibacy/continence; 'purity' here is technical term for sexual abstinence.

notes.quote: If he is recognized more highly than the bishop, he has been corrupted.
notes.why: 'Recognized' is passive but agent is unclear; means 'if he is esteemed/valued more highly.'
notes.fix: 'If he is held in higher esteem than the bishop.'

notes.quote: If he is recognized more highly than the bishop
notes.why: Repeated from garbled; 'recognized' is weak for 'esteemed.'

polish.changed: Clarified the implied subject of the opening commands, kept the compressed logic of the continence warning intact, and preserved all qualifications and Scripture references exactly.

notes.quote: If he is esteemed more highly than the bishop, he has been corrupted
notes.why: Logic is compressed; means 'if continence leads to pride above the bishop'.
notes.fix: Add note: ascetic pride that disregards the bishop's authority is corruption.

polish.changed: Clarified the compressed logic about continence and the bishop by rendering 'known more than the bishop' as 'esteemed more highly than the bishop,' making the warning about boasting above episcopal authority easier to follow.

notes.quote: If he is esteemed more highly than the bishop, he has been corrupted
notes.why: Logic is compressed: continence boasted of above bishop's authority corrupts.
notes.fix: 'If he boasts of being more highly esteemed than the bishop'.
